diff.description: The first utility is composed of the available space in the cell (yard_cells and street_cells) minus the elements which decreases the cells's utility (num_areas, green_space, num_trees, uhei). It's a really simple and intuitive function, which can be used as a comparison with the results for the others.

default.description: In the default configutations equal weights have been assigned to the different elements of the macro factor.

higher density.description: The density enhanced configuration is set with a much greater weight for the population density factor with respect to the others.

higher green.description: The green enhanced configuration is set with a much greater weight for the green factor with respect to the others.

higher uhei.description: This configuration assign more importance to the uhei factor. The uhei enhanced configuration gives more importance to the uhei factor. This is probably the fairest configuration, since it can be viewed as a summary of multiple informations.

no street.description: The no street configuration shows the results without consider the availability to place new green areas on the roads.

no yard.description: The no yard configuration shows the results without consider the availability to place new green areas on yards..

inverse uhei.description: This utility function focuses on lowering the heat island risk by evaluating the impact of the green on the Inverse UHEI (IUHEI). Contrarily to the UHEI, the lower is the index value, the higher is the risk and it means also that the lower is the amount of existing vegetation.

ndvi.description: This utility function maximizes the green impact on the NDVI, which is strictly correlated to the green and is a normalized index, so it is easier to manage with respect to the UHEI. The improvement given by new cells is scaled according to the observed data and the higher the value, the greener the cell is.
